note: A SCRATCH catalogue, not the main one. It exists to answer the single question F028 left open: R4's proof perimeter is five Gobra-verified packages, R5's refinement perimeter is four clause-carrying files, and the only file between them is internal/dom/dom.go -- but the main catalogue has no mutant confined to that file, so the two columns agreed on all 18 cells without ever being given a chance to disagree. Two of these mutants are confined to internal/dom/dom.go and to nothing else, and separate the columns by REACH (F038). The third, clock-now-off-by-one, is inside a file R5 DOES reach and separates them by VERDICT (F039). They are deliberately NOT in tools/cmd/mutate/mutants.json: the ids there are shared across all four corners so the kill table can compare a defect port-to-port, and a Go-only id would break that symmetry and shift every published denominator to settle a question about one rung pair. Run with `calibrate -manifest evidence/experiments/r4-r5-separation/manifest.json -impls go -rungs R4,R5`.

families.validation: observable input validation inside the verified core: the handle alphabet (D1) and the text character range (D6). Both are proved in internal/dom/dom.go by a loop invariant that cannot be restated in the postcondition, so they are obligations R4 can see and the refinement clause list cannot.
families.attribution: a defect inside a file that DOES carry refinement clauses, but on a member that does not. R4 and R5 separate by VERDICT here rather than by reach: R5's perimeter includes the file, the refinement clause list has no clause for the broken obligation, and the attribution engine reads Gobra's own error and declines the kill.

mutants.description: ValidHandle accepts the byte range A..z instead of a..z, so uppercase handles and the punctuation between Z and a ([, \, ], ^, `) are admitted -- handle "Alice" registers. Breaks the third loop invariant of ValidHandle, which is the only place the alphabet property is proved.

ValidText drops the control-character guard, so a tweet body containing a NUL or a newline is accepted and echoed back. Breaks the third loop invariant of ValidText, which is the only place the character-range property is proved.

(*clock.Logical).Now returns l.now + 1, so every tweet's created_at is one ahead of the clock. The edit is INSIDE internal/clock/clock.go, which is in r5Files, so R5 reaches it -- but clock.go's only refinement clause site sits on (*Logical).Tick, and the failing postcondition is Now's own. R4 and R5 therefore differ by VERDICT rather than by reach.
